title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
key_facts: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, three OpenAI safety researchers fired the week before, published an open letter on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
The letter went to OpenAI's Safety and Security Committee, Safety Advisory Group and Mission Advisory Council.
OpenAI said they violated policy by 'accessing and handling sensitive company information'; a spokesperson told TechCrunch an investigation found a 'pattern of misconduct'.
The three deny mishandling information and deny involvement in a leak to The Information about less monitorable model architectures.
Wang says OpenAI told her she was fired for opening an executive's email, access that OpenAI had delegated to her for recruiting; she says she reported it within minutes.
OpenAI has not formally answered the letter; an internal memo shared with TechCrunch says the firings were not about raising safety concerns.
OpenAI did not say which policies were broken or how it protects staff who raise safety concerns.
quote_evidence: The researchers were dismissed last week after allegedly sharing confidential company information with a third-party AI safety organization.

OpenAI has not formally responded to the open letter, but shared with TechCrunch an internal memo attributed to a research leader, praising the three researchers’ contributions to AI safety and denying that they were fired in retaliation.

OpenAI did not directly address TechCrunch’s questions about specifically which policies the researchers allegedly violated, the circumstances of their dismissal, or how the company protects employees who raise safety concerns and collaborate with external evaluators.
why_it_matters_hint: The dispute shows how unclear the rules are for safety staff who work with outside experts at a leading AI lab.
event_date: Open letter published Thursday 8 Oct 2026; firings the week before.
notes: Full TechCrunch text read. Two sides disagree; nothing independently verified.
